headline: Fasting raises GH
punch: Both are true at the same time.

headline: You have seen the claim
body: So it gets repeated constantly that fasting raises growth hormone, usually as an argument for why fasting is good for you. The GH part is accurate. GH genuinely does go up and the measurements are solid. | What gets left off every single time is what happens to everything downstream of that GH, and the answer is the exact opposite of what the rising GH number would lead you to expect.
punch: GH up. Now follow it downstream.

headline: So why does IGF-1 fall?
body: Energy deficit downregulates hepatic **GH receptor** expression. The signal keeps arriving, in larger amounts than normal, and there is progressively less on the liver surface to catch it with. | That state has a name in the literature: **acquired GH resistance**. GH rises and IGF-1 falls anyway, in the same animal at the same time, because the step connecting them has been broken rather than because the signal got weaker.

headline: Three brakes
body: First, fewer GH receptors on the liver surface, which is the main one. Second, low insulin raises *IGFBP-1*, which binds up free IGF-1 and removes it from play, exactly the mechanism from the insulin post. | And third, protein-calorie malnutrition can induce proteins that block hepatic GH signal transduction by inhibiting the JAK/STAT pathway directly. Three separate mechanisms, all pointing the same direction at once.
punch: Three brakes between GH and IGF-1.

headline: Farnum 2003
body: Four-week-old male rats, **3 days** of fasting, then bone elongation measured directly at the growth plate rather than inferred from hormones. | The proximal tibial plate dropped to **30% of control**. And the distal tibial plate **stopped growing altogether**. Two growth plates in the same leg, in the same animal, under the same energy deficit, responding completely differently.
punch: _Two plates in one leg. One slowed. One stopped._

headline: Why did the smaller plate stop?
body: The distal tibial plate contributes less length than the proximal one does. Under energy stress, the smaller contributor shut down first and completely, while the larger one kept running at a reduced rate. | That is the same ordering the bone age work showed on a different question: plates are not one system responding together. They are separate systems with separate priorities, and the body appears to rank them.

headline: Then they refed
body: Both growth plates were back to control growth rates by **7 days** after the fast ended, and weight was back to 95% of controls by 28 days. Fast recovery, which you would expect. | But the proximal plate did not stop at control. It ran **10 to 15% above control** for the rest of the experimental period. The catch-up overshot normal and stayed there, which tells you the plate was not simply running down a fixed clock.
punch: ==Catch-up did not stop at normal. It overshot.==

headline: In humans it is fast
body: IGF-1 fell in prepubertal children after just **six days** of either 50% calorie restriction or 33% protein restriction. Six days, not six months, and in the population where it matters most. | What this means is that the axis reports energy availability on a timescale of days. It is not a slow adaptation to chronic undernutrition. It responds to this week.
punch: Six days moved it in children.

headline: Be precise about duration
body: The rodent work suggests it takes roughly **3 days** of actual fasting, not an overnight fast, to meaningfully collapse growth plate output. | So an overnight fast and a three-day fast are not the same intervention being discussed at two different lengths. They are different things, and nothing in this data says anything about skipping breakfast.

headline: One real counterexample
body: A 2-year human trial of 25% calorie restriction in adults found that sustained restriction **did not significantly lower IGF-1**, which the authors attributed to the trial's high protein intake. | So calories alone do not settle this. Protein intake appears to protect the axis somewhat independently of energy balance, and anyone quoting the fasting-lowers-IGF-1 line should know this trial exists and contradicts the simple version.

headline: What to take from this
body: Fasting genuinely raises GH and genuinely lowers IGF-1, because it breaks the step between them rather than because it weakens the signal. The growth plate follows IGF-1, not GH, so the plate slows while the headline hormone climbs. | And the recovery overshoots control, which is the clearest demonstration in this series that the plate is not simply counting down a fixed allowance.
punch: ==A higher GH number can mean less growth, not more.==
